findings.title: Team admin check uses `&&` instead of `||`
findings.body: `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed as `(await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))`. Because `isTeamAdmin` and `isTeamOwner` check for distinct roles (`ADMIN` vs `OWNER`) or require both conditions to be true simultaneously, a user who is only a team admin (and not the team owner) will fail this check and receive a `FORBIDDEN` error when trying to add guests to a team booking. This should use `||` instead of `&&`.

findings.title: Calendar update uses caller's credentials instead of the booking organizer's credentials
findings.body: `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)` and `new EventManager({ ...user, credentials })` use the currently logged-in caller (`ctx.user`) rather than the booking's organizer (`booking.user`). `addGuestsHandler` explicitly allows attendees and team admins/owners (who are not the organizer) to add guests. When an attendee or team admin invokes `addGuests`, `EventManager` is initialized with their credentials instead of the organizer's, so `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` will fail to update the organizer's external calendar event (or attempt the update against the wrong account).

findings.title: `prisma.user.findFirstOrThrow` with `id: booking.userId || 0` can return an arbitrary user or throw when `booking.userId` is null
findings.body: When `booking.userId` is `null` or `0`, `where: { id: booking.userId || 0 }` queries for a user with `id: 0`, which will throw `NotFoundError` (an unhandled 500 error instead of a proper `TRPCError`). Additionally, `booking.user` is already fetched in the initial `prisma.booking.findFirst` query (lines 35-40), so this extra query is redundant if `booking.user` is selected with the needed fields.

findings.title: Duplicate emails in `input.guests` and case differences bypass deduplication and blacklist checks
findings.body: `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` on the server (`addGuests.schema.ts`) does not enforce uniqueness or lowercase normalization on `guests`. If a client calls the TRPC endpoint directly with duplicate emails in `guests` (e.g. `['a@b.com', 'a@b.com']`), both pass the `uniqueGuests` filter and duplicate attendee records are created in the database. Furthermore, `blacklistedGuestEmails` is lowercased, but `guest` and `attendee.email` are compared without lowercasing, so mixed-case emails bypass both the blacklist check and existing attendee check.

findings.title: `sendAddGuestsEmails` ignores event type email disable settings (`disableStandardEmails`)
findings.body: Unlike `sendScheduledEmails`, `sendRescheduledEmails`, and `sendLocationChangeEmails` right above it, `sendAddGuestsEmails` does not accept `eventTypeMetadata` or check `eventTypeDisableHostEmail(eventTypeMetadata)` and `eventTypeDisableAttendeeEmail(eventTypeMetadata)`. Event types configured to suppress standard host or attendee emails will still send emails when guests are added.
